name: CO-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Kiros has raised over $1 million; Republican under $3,000
model.rationale: Denver-based CO-01 is one of the most Democratic districts in the country, and the Democratic nominee has vastly outraised a Republican who has essentially no campaign resources. Markets price this as a near-certain Democratic hold, consistent with the district's fundamentals.
model.watch: A major late outside-spending surge for the Republican or an unexpected scandal involving the Democratic nominee would be the main way this moves.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Diana DeGette (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Denver's CO-01 is an open seat after longtime incumbent Diana DeGette left the ballot, but the district's D+29 partisan lean makes it among the most Democratic seats in the nation. Melat Kiros enters the general election with more than $1 million raised and substantial outside spending on both sides, while Republican Christy Peterson has raised roughly $2,000 and shows no meaningful campaign infrastructure.

Prediction markets give the Democratic nominee about a 97% chance of winning, and no independent or third-party candidates appear positioned to alter the outcome. The forecast treats this as a Safe Democratic hold, with the expected margin near the district's underlying partisan lean.
